problems.title: Combine cube roots before multiplying
problems.question: Simplify $\frac{\sqrt[3]{(\sqrt2-\sqrt{10})^2}}{\sqrt[3]{\sqrt{10}+\sqrt2}}\frac{\sqrt5+1}{\sqrt2}$.
problems.idea: Use the conjugate product (√10−√2)(√10+√2)=8.
steps: Taking its real cube root gives (√10−√2)/2.

problems.title: A diagonal divides a trapezoid’s altitude
problems.question: In a right trapezoid, the longer diagonal divides the altitude from the obtuse vertex into lengths 5 cm and 3 cm. The longer leg equals the smaller base. Find the area.
problems.idea: The altitude is 8; use similar triangles along the longer diagonal.
formulas: Let larger base B, smaller base b, height h=8. The lower altitude piece is 8b/B.
steps: The lower altitude piece is either 5 or 3, so b/B is either 5/8 or 3/8.
The leg equation simplifies to B²(2b/B−1)=64; positivity forces b/B>1/2. Thus b/B=5/8.
Then B²/4=64, so B=16, b=10.

problems.title: Fifth roots of equal and opposite numbers
problems.question: Simplify $(\sqrt[5]{9\sqrt3}+\sqrt[5]{-27/\sqrt3})^4$.
problems.idea: Both radicands have the same magnitude.
steps: Odd roots preserve the sign. The two fifth roots are √3 and −√3.
Their sum is 0, whose fourth power is 0.

problems.title: An equation involving the floor function
problems.question: Solve ⌊b²−2b+3⌋=2.
problems.idea: A floor of 2 means the expression is at least 2 and less than 3.
steps: The lower inequality is automatic. The upper gives (b−1)²<1.
Therefore −1<b−1<1.

problems.title: The shaded triangle in a rectangle
problems.question: In rectangle ABCD, AM:MB=1:2 and BN:NC=3:1. Find shaded area MND divided by the unshaded area.
problems.idea: Subtract the three corner triangles from the whole rectangle.
formulas: Normalize rectangle area to 1; triangle area=base×height/2.
steps: Triangle AMD has area 1/6. Triangle BMN has area (2/3)(3/4)/2=1/4. Triangle NCD has area 1/8.
Their total is 13/24, so the shaded triangle has area 11/24.
The required ratio is (11/24)/(13/24).

problems.title: Place a number strictly between two quadratic roots
problems.question: For which a does x²−(a−1)x+a²−10=0 have one root above −3 and one below −3?
problems.idea: A monic quadratic is negative strictly between its two real roots.
steps: The necessary and sufficient condition is f(−3)<0. It also guarantees two distinct real roots.
The product is negative between its roots −4 and 1.

problems.title: Integer parameters giving opposite-sign roots
problems.question: How many integer a make ax²−(a−1)x+a³−20a=0 a quadratic with opposite-sign roots?
problems.idea: Opposite-sign roots have negative product.
steps: Require a²<20. The integer possibilities are −4,−3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3,4.
Remove a=0 because then the equation is not quadratic.

problems.title: Map an interval through a reciprocal function
problems.question: The range of f is [−3,5]. How many integers are in the range of y=(8−f(x))/(7+f(x))?
problems.idea: Set t=f(x) and find the endpoint values.
steps: As t increases from −3 to 5, this expression decreases continuously from 11/4 to 1/4.
Its range is [1/4,11/4], containing exactly 1 and 2.

problems.title: An area ratio using a parallel line
problems.question: In triangle ABC, BM:MC=1:3, AN:NC=3:2, and MT∥BN with T on AC. Find area ABN divided by area MCT.
problems.idea: Choose convenient coordinates; affine coordinates preserve area ratios.
steps: M=(3/4,1/4), N=(0,3/5). The line through M parallel to BN meets AC at T=(0,7/10).
Their ratio is (3/10)/(9/80)=8/3.

problems.title: An intersection and a second area ratio
problems.question: Use the same configuration BM:MC=1:3, AN:NC=3:2, MT∥BN. If K=AM∩BN, find area ABC divided by area AKN.
problems.idea: Find K with two linear equations.
steps: Solving gives K=(9/14,3/14).
Area AKN=(3/5)(9/14)/2=27/140, while area ABC=1/2.

problems.title: Equilateral triangles and a square area ratio
problems.question: Areas of two equilateral triangles are in ratio 4:25. Their side lengths differ by 21 cm. Find the sum of their sides.
problems.idea: For similar figures, side ratio is the square root of area ratio.
steps: Write the sides as 2k and 5k. Then 3k=21, so k=7.
The side sum is 7k.

problems.title: Construct an odd function from any function
problems.question: Which listed expression is odd for every real function f defined on all real numbers?
problems.idea: An odd function g satisfies g(−x)=−g(x).
steps: Then g(−x)=f(−x)−f(x)=−g(x).
Thus this difference always works, without any assumption about f.

problems.title: Even roots need absolute values
problems.question: For $-1<x<0$, the sum $\sqrt[4]{x^4(x+2)^8/(x+2)^4}+\sqrt[3]{x^3(x+2)^5/(x+2)^2}$ is p. Find p.
problems.idea: An even root returns a nonnegative value.
formulas: First term=|x|(x+2); second term=x(x+2), since x+2>0.
steps: Because x<0, |x|=−x.
The terms cancel: −x(x+2)+x(x+2)=0.

problems.title: A difference of cubes
problems.question: If ∛x−∛y=1 and xy=8, find x−y.
problems.idea: Put u=∛x and v=∛y.
steps: Substitute to get x−y=1·(1+6).

problems.title: Distance from the centroid to an equilateral side
problems.question: In an equilateral triangle, the intersection of the medians is distance 1 from a side. Find the perimeter.
problems.idea: For an equilateral triangle the centroid is also the incenter.
steps: r=1 gives h=3 and s=2√3.
Multiply by 3 for the perimeter.

problems.title: A missing value of a rational function
problems.question: Find the range of y=(2x−1)/(5x+4).
problems.idea: Solve for x in terms of y.
steps: If y=2/5, this equation becomes 0=−13/5, impossible.
Every other y gives x=(−1−4y)/(5y−2), and this never equals the forbidden input −4/5.

problems.title: The inradius of a tangential isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has an incircle, acute angle 45° and area 36√2. Find its inradius.
problems.idea: Use tangency to replace the sum of bases by the sum of legs.
steps: Thus S=h²√2=36√2, giving h=6.
The incircle touches the two parallel bases, so 2r=h.

problems.title: A function decreasing on its whole domain
problems.question: Among −x², −x³, (x−1)/(x+4), −|x|, 7, 2x−10, how many are decreasing functions?
problems.idea: Check whether increasing the input always lowers the output.
steps: Only −x³ is strictly decreasing throughout its domain.
−x² and −|x| change direction; 7 is constant; 2x−10 increases.
The rational expression equals 1−5/(x+4) and increases on each side of its pole.

problems.title: Extend a formula evenly
problems.question: f is even, and f(x)=x²−3x for x≥0. Solve f(x)>0.
problems.idea: Replace the nonnegative input by |x|.
steps: This is positive exactly when |x|>3.

problems.title: Three shaded triangles in a rhombus
problems.question: M,N are midpoints of CD,AD in rhombus ABCD. Find the fraction of the rhombus shaded in the printed diagram.
problems.idea: Use affine coordinates and the intersections of BM,BN with AC.
formulas: Normalize A=(0,0),B=(1,0),D=(0,1),C=(1,1); areas scale by the same factor.
steps: Then M=(1/2,1),N=(0,1/2). The intersections with AC are X=(2/3,2/3) and Y=(1/3,1/3).
The shaded pieces are BXY, CMX and ANY. Their normalized areas are 1/6,1/12,1/12.
Their sum is 1/3 of the whole rhombus.

problems.title: Sum of distances to equilateral sides
problems.question: An equilateral triangle has side 6. An interior point is distances 1 and 2 from AB and AC. Find its distance from BC.
problems.idea: Split the triangle into three triangles with the same base length.
formulas: For an interior point, d₁+d₂+d₃=h; h=s√3/2.
steps: The altitude is 3√3.
Thus the third distance is 3√3−1−2.

problems.title: Complete a square in an absolute value
problems.question: Find the minimum of f(x)=x²−|2x|−8.
problems.idea: Set t=|x|≥0.
steps: The square is zero at t=1.
Both x=1 and x=−1 attain the minimum.

problems.title: Count intersections with a fractional-part function
problems.question: How many real roots satisfy {x}=−0.25x+0.5, where {x} is the fractional part?
problems.idea: Write x=n+t, with n an integer and 0≤t<1.
steps: The restriction 0≤(2−n)/5<1 gives −3<n≤2.
The five integer n values are −2,−1,0,1,2. Each gives exactly one valid x=n+t.

problems.title: Symmetry gives a root average
problems.question: Find the arithmetic mean of all real roots of $x^4-2/x^2=(7-9x^2)/(|x|+1)$.
problems.idea: The equation is unchanged when x is replaced by −x.
formulas: Its domain excludes 0; any nonzero root occurs with its opposite.
steps: For positive x, left side minus right side tends to −∞ near 0 and to +∞ for large x, so at least one root exists.
Multiplying by x²(|x|+1) gives a nonzero polynomial on each half-axis, so there are only finitely many roots.
Pair every positive root with its negative. Their sum, and hence their average, is zero.

problems.title: An odd-function expression collapses
problems.question: f is odd and f(3)+f(−5)=7. Find 7f(3)+8f(−5)+2f(−3)+3f(5).
problems.idea: Replace negative inputs using oddness.
steps: The expression becomes (7−2)f(3)+(8−3)f(−5).
